critical_code_review_comments: inbox.py score_message: catches ALL exceptions with bare `except Exception` and only logger.exception's, so a persistently failing scoring service leaves messages with score=None indefinitely (they'll re-attempt only when /inbox/score is manually invoked). Consider a retry count field or scored_attempts, so pathologically bad messages don't burn Claude credits on every batch call.

inbox.py public_contact: no rate limiting / captcha. A bot could hammer /api/public/contact/{token} and burn EMERGENT_LLM_KEY credits via the score_message task. Recommend per-IP rate limit (e.g., 5/min) or a simple honeypot field.

inbox.py score_inbox limits pending to 15 with .limit(15) but 'remaining' recounts count_documents so accurate. However, the asyncio.gather fans out up to 15 concurrent Claude calls which could hit rate limits — consider a semaphore(3-5).

InboxPanel.jsx line 8 ScoreBadge: when score==null it emits a fragment/nothing (implicit false), meaning unscored messages have NO badge at all. Users won't know why some rows lack badges. Consider a subtle '—' or 'pending' badge for score==null so intent is obvious.

PageTransition.jsx uses exit={{opacity:0,y:-8}} but AnimatePresence in App.js uses mode='wait' which fully unmounts the old page before mounting the new one — this is fine but the 280ms delay is user-perceptible when navigating quickly (e.g., double-click tabs). Not a bug, just UX note.
